summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to move data to separate systems for inference, embedding generation, and similarity search. Native vector search and LLM integration are now common, with platforms like Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML, and Databricks Mosaic AI offering managed access to foundation models alongside SQL. By 2026, roughly 75% of enterprise AI applications are expected to depend on vector search capabilities, with general-purpose databases such as PostgreSQL gaining ground while purpose-built vector databases narrow to high-performance niches.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides fully managed LLM and ML functions callable directly from SQL, including text completion, summarization, sentiment analysis, translation, and embedding generation. It integrates serverless access to hosted foundation models (e.g., from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and Snowflake's own Arctic) and extends to Snowflake Postgres so developers can run AI functions alongside transactional Postgres data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the VECTOR data type and VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / vector similarity functions. In Snowflake Postgres, vector storage and semantic search are natively supported as part of the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native LLM integration through Cortex functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, EMBED_TEXT) and Cortex Analyst/Search, offering managed access to multiple third-party and first-party foundation models without external API management.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing measured in credits; Cortex functions are billed per token/compute consumed on top of standard Snowflake compute and storage costs.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, and more) using standard SQL, and integrates with Vertex AI to invoke Gemini and other foundation models for generative tasks, text generation, and embeddings directly in queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH function and vector indexes (ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING for creating embeddings, CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest-neighbor search).
databases.llm_integration: Strong native integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models through remote models and ML.GENERATE_TEXT / ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions, enabling generative AI and embeddings from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (bytes scanned) or flat-rate/capacity pricing; ML model creation and inference incur additional BigQuery ML charges, and Vertex AI model calls are billed separately via Vertex AI.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search, while pgai (from Timescale) brings embedding creation and LLM calls (e.g., to OpenAI, Ollama) directly into SQL workflows, letting teams keep AI data and operations alongside relational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Vector search is provided via the pgvector extension rather than the core database engine. For a vanilla PostgreSQL install, vector search requires installing pgvector; it is extremely widely adopted but technically an extension, not a native core feature. (Note: Snowflake Postgres and some managed offerings expose it more natively.)
databases.llm_integration: LLM integration via the pgai extension, which enables embedding generation and model inference calls to providers like OpenAI, Cohere, and local models directly from SQL; otherwise handled in the application layer.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL and pgvector/pgai are open source and free; costs come from self-hosting infrastructure or managed provider fees (e.g., Timescale, AWS, GCP) plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML enables SQL-based inference by integrating Amazon Aurora with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock, allowing queries to call ML models and generative AI (including LLMs and embeddings) directly from SQL functions without exporting data.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector search in Aurora's core engine. On Aurora PostgreSQL, vector search is available only through the pgvector extension; Aurora ML itself does not provide built-in vector indexing, so this is marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI (text generation, embeddings) and SageMaker for custom models, invoked via SQL functions in Aurora.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/IO pricing applies; ML inference calls incur separate SageMaker or Bedrock charges based on usage.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML allows users to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL by integrating with Amazon SageMaker (including Autopilot), and supports invoking Bedrock LLMs for generative AI tasks on data warehouse data directly from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native built-in vector search / vector index in Redshift's core engine. Vector similarity can be approximated using data type storage and distance computations, and Redshift integrates with Bedrock for embeddings, but there is no dedicated native ANN vector search feature, so this is marked false.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with SageMaker for model training/inference and Amazon Bedrock for LLM and embedding functions callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed via Redshift provisioned or serverless compute and storage; model training/inference uses SageMaker resources billed separately, and Bedrock calls are charged per usage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform through Mosaic AI, covering model training, fine-tuning, serving, agent development, and GenAI governance, combined with Databricks Vector Search for retrieval-augmented generation on data in the lakehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via Databricks Vector Search, a managed service that creates and syncs vector indexes from Delta tables with automatic embedding computation and governance via Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Comprehensive native LLM integration through Mosaic AI Model Serving, Foundation Model APIs, agent frameworks, and support for open and proprietary models plus fine-tuning.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) across compute, model serving, and vector search; serverless model endpoints and vector search are billed per usage on top of underlying cloud compute.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables semantic and similarity search over embeddings stored directly alongside operational document data, supporting RAG applications and AI-powered features within the same Atlas cluster.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search integrated into the Atlas platform via vector search indexes and the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, supporting approximate nearest-neighbor search with hybrid (keyword + vector) capabilities.
databases.llm_integration: No in-database LLM hosting, but integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex AI, etc.) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing on dedicated tiers; vector search consumes cluster compute/memory resources, with dedicated Search Nodes optionally provisioned and billed separately for scaling.
